text:
maya: Heads up — after the gpu-operator (v1.14.0) rollout in us-east-1 we're seeing a cluster-wide scheduling backlog for GPU pods, a bunch stuck Pending with no allocatable GPUs. :frowning_face:

luis: Confirmed, noticed ~40 pods Pending across dedicated-pool-us-east. Some nodes report device plugin registration but no driver reported.

ash: Logs from one affected node: 
```
Jan 12 09:12:21 gpu-node-17 kubelet[2345]: deviceplugin: failed to register: driver-version mismatch (cuda:11.8 / kernel-module: 470.XX)
Jan 12 09:12:21 gpu-node-17 kernel: nvidia: module license 'NVIDIA' taints kernel
Jan 12 09:12:21 gpu-node-17 systemd: dkms: ERROR: could not build module for kernel 5.15.0-102
```

maya: infra-bot already fired an alert: "driver-registration-race" on gpu-node-17, gpu-node-18.

infra-bot: Automated alert: GPU driver/module mismatch detected on nodes [gpu-node-17,gpu-node-18]. Suggested action: cordon + drain and reinstall kernel headers/drivers.

raj: Quick hypothesis: gpu-operator device-plugin changed registration ordering so device-plugin advertises before driver module finished probing -> scheduler sees GPU resource but node advertising is inconsistent leading to bin-packing/race. Could also be dkms rebuild failures after recent kernel roll.

luis: I see two correlated events: kernel security patches landed and we rolled nodepool OS to 5.15.0-102 earlier this morning, and gpu-operator rollout happened ~5m later. Timing likely triggered driver-module build failures.

ash: Repro steps I ran on a canary node: reboot -> kubelet starts -> device-plugin container starts, emits /var/log/device-plugin errors, DKMS fails to build nvidia module because headers package missing. Running `modprobe nvidia` fails.

ash: Commands that helped inspect: 
```
kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu-node-1
kubectl describe node gpu-node-17
journalctl -u kubelet -u device-plugin -n 200 | grep -i nvidia
```

maya: Mitigation plan in chat: 1) Pause gpu-operator rollout, 2) cordon unhealthy nodes, 3) drain impacted nodes to fallback pool, 4) manually reinstall kernel-headers + re-trigger dkms build, 5) verify device-plugin logs show stable registration, 6) uncordon.

oncall-sre: I'm on it — cordoning gpu-node-17/18/19. Draining to fallback-gpu-pool. Will run driver install script from runbooks. FYI this will cause short interruptions for running ML jobs.

raj: For longer-term fix: we should update the gpu-operator helm chart to wait-for-driver-init before advertising resources (or move device-plugin to init container that blocks until /dev/nvidia0 exists). Also add a dkms preflight that ensures kernel-headers present before kernel upgrade completes.

luis: Agree. Also need a canary strategy: roll kernel upgrades out to 5 nodes, wait 30m, then continue. Right now dedicated capacity underutilized and we're still paying the reserved pool cost — if this stretches beyond a day we should re-balance jobs or spin up temporary spot capacity in another zone. Cost ops: ops-fin warned about committed spend while utilization drops.

maya: For immediate rollback I'm proposing: rollback gpu-operator to v1.13.2 in us-east-1 while we patch chart. Can we do a fast rollback?

ash: We can `helm rollback` across the nodepool namespace but it's messy if some device-plugin pods are already running new image. Better: cordon nodes, uninstall operator on those nodes, redeploy previous daemonset image tag, then uncordon after validated. I'll script it.

infra-bot: Deploy bot: rollback request queued for namespace gpu-system-us-east. Running preflight checks.

oncall-sre: Manual driver reinstall completed on gpu-node-17, device-plugin now shows: `Registered resource name: nvidia.com/gpu count: 4` and pods scheduled. Re-running healthcheck.

luis: Good sign. I'm seeing scheduling clear up on ~60% of pending pods after drains. Still ~10 pods pending due to quota.

raj: Action items: 
- ash to open PR updating operator chart to add driver-init wait (include init container patch).
- infra to add kernel-header preflight in cluster-upgrade job.
- ops to implement staged kernel rollouts with canary + health-check gates.
- finance/ops to review committed-capacity exposure if pools remain underutilized >24h.

maya: ETA: we'll keep rollback in place for next 2h, if stable we'll resume controlled rollout with the init workaround. Will post updates. :thumbsup:

ash: Note for postmortem: include exact dkms logs and timeline of node pool OS rollout + gpu-operator release. Also add a note about NCCL behavior — if driver mismatch persisted across a rack, we might see degraded NCCL rings (jobs report hangs). I captured a failing mpi run stacktrace; adding to incident artifacts.

oncall-sre: Closing loop: all nodes in dedicated-pool-us-east revalidated, scheduling normalized, rolling back gpu-operator to v1.13.2 done. Marking incident as mitigated, will follow up with RFC for chart change.

maya: Thanks everyone. Please add any leftover notes to the incident doc and PRs. :raised_hands:
